note: Known-answer findings, one per detection method. Each says what it is findable by and what it is invisible to, so a negative result can be told apart from a missed one.

findings.findable_by: metadata: one message to an address that appears once in the corpus
findings.invisible_to: content analysis: a two-word body and an attachment that will not open
findings.expected_answer: m.delacroix@harbor-line-consulting.invalid is a single-document entity in Key Relationships, on one outbound message from Michael Brennan carrying an encrypted attachment. Nothing in the text says so.
findings.how_to_verify: Key Relationships: the address appears as a non-custodian entity with exactly one document. Searching the extracted text for it returns the one email and nothing else.

findings.invisible_to: every keyword filter on the matter, and every metadata cut
findings.expected_answer: A contemporaneous note describing a decision kept out of writing. It names no company, no file and no person in full, and hits none of the matter's search terms.
findings.how_to_verify: Search the extracted text for any matter keyword: this document is not in the results. It is reachable only through a topic or summary pass, or by a reviewer opening it.
findings.body:
Notes from Thursday.

He was clear that the number should not move again before the end of the quarter,
and that nobody outside the room needs to see the working. I said I would keep my
own copy of the earlier version. J. will take the part that touches the field team,
so it stays out of my folder.

If anyone asks later, the decision was made in the room and not in writing. That
was the point of doing it that way.

I am not putting the rest of this in an email.

findings.findable_by: the same filter that catches the principal
findings.invisible_to: nothing — it is meant to be caught

distinguisher.why: A second message to the same address explains it: an external assurance provider on an internal controls review, working papers returned encrypted. The address therefore appears twice, and the principal's appears once.

findings.expected_answer: r.okafor@ledgerline-assurance.invalid matches the principal's pattern and is innocent. The right answer is reached by walking the entity's other documents, not by reading this one.
findings.how_to_verify: Key Relationships: this entity carries two documents, not one. Open the second and the encrypted attachment is accounted for.
findings.body: As discussed. Attached, same password as last time.
findings.distinguisher_body:
Confirming the walkthrough for Thursday at 2pm.

Our external assurance provider will attend. Their engagement letter for the
internal controls review is on file with the finance team, and the working papers
come back to us encrypted as usual. Nothing in scope for the litigation hold.

Please have the reconciliation ready.

findings.findable_by: full extraction: the payload is on tab 11 of 12, 'Reconciliation'
findings.invisible_to: any extraction that stops at the first sheet
findings.expected_answer: Three released orders with no documented justification, on the 'Reconciliation' tab. The first tab is a clean summary.
findings.how_to_verify: Search the extracted text for 'without documented justification'. A hit means the whole workbook was read.
payload_rows: Released without documented justification — flag cleared manually
Released without documented justification — flag cleared manually
Threshold raised after release, no approval on file

findings.findable_by: the pair itself: they correspond at volume, so the edge is real
findings.invisible_to: any topical link to the matter, because there is none
findings.expected_answer: Thomas Bradley and Gregory Nash exchange 18 documents, every one of them about an employee blood drive. They share no issue tag, and the vocabulary of that correspondence appears in no other document. Asked what connects them, the answer is one mundane subject. Asked whether they discuss the matter, the answer is no, and that is correct rather than a gap.
findings.how_to_verify: Key Relationships: the pair has a real edge with real volume. Search the extracted text of those documents for any matter keyword: no hits. Search the corpus for 'blood drive': only these.
